title: How often pastors speak about mental illness in sermons
subtitle: U.S. Protestant pastors, 2014 and 2021 surveys
caption: Fewer pastors rarely or never raise the subject than in 2014, and more raise it several times a year or more. Still, more than a third rarely or never bring it up from the pulpit.
note: Pastors were asked how often they speak to their church in sermons or large group messages about mental illness. The 2014 question asked about "acute mental illness"; the 2021 question asked about "acute or chronic mental illness", so the wording is not identical. In 2021, 17% said about once a year and 3% were not sure. The 2021 survey was released in 2022.

rows.label: Several times a year or more

sources.study: Pastors Have Congregational and, for Some, Personal Experience With Mental Illness
sources.field_dates: Phone survey, Sept. 1 to 29, 2021; the 2014 comparison figures, as printed in this release and its full report, come from Lifeway's phone survey of 1,000 Protestant pastors, May 7 to 31, 2014
sources.sample: 1,000 U.S. Protestant pastors; margin of error plus or minus 3.2 points, higher in subgroups
